articles.title: 'Todos esperavam' que eleição no Brasil fosse para 2º turno, diz secretário de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, falou sobre pleito brasileiro nesta segunda (5) e não citou nenhum dos candidatos. Donald Trump também citou eleição e confundiu a Índia com o Brasil. Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula disputarão presidência em 25 de outubro.
articles.summary: Secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, falou sobre pleito brasileiro nesta segunda (5) e não citou nenhum dos candidatos. Donald Trump também citou eleição e confundiu a Índia com o Brasil. Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula disputarão presidência em 25 de outubro.
articles.body:
Secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos , Marco Rubio , falou nesta segunda-feira (5) sobre a eleição brasileira e disse que "todos esperavam" que o pleito fosse para o 2º turno. Ele indicou também que o governo Trump acompanhará a nova disputa entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula em 25 de outubro.

"Foi para o 2º turno e todos esperavam que isso fosse acontecer. Vamos ver como as coisas se desenrolam", afirmou Rubio em entrevista a jornalistas antes de embarcar para a Islândia. Sua resposta foi sucinta e durou menos de 10 segundos, e ele não citou nenhum dos candidatos.

O senador Flávio Bolsonaro e o presidente Lula foram ao 2º turno em votação no domingo. O político do PL obteve cerca de 47% dos votos, enquanto o líder petista teve pouco mais de 45% dos votos. (Leia mais abaixo)

O governo Trump tem evitado falar muito sobre as eleições brasileiras e tampouco declarar uma eventual preferência a um dos candidatos, apesar de ter uma afinidade ideológica com Flávio Bolsonaro. Em declarações anteriores, o presidente Donald Trump afirmou que acompanha o pleito "bem de perto".

Trump elogia rapidez da eleição brasileira e confunde Brasil com Índia

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, em 28 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, confundiu o Brasil com a Índia ao citar a eleição presidencial brasileira nas redes sociais nesta segunda-feira (5).

A publicação foi corrigida horas depois e passou a citar corretamente o Brasil. Ele elogiou a rapidez da apuração no pleito brasileiro e não mencionou nem Flávio Bolsonaro nem o presidente Lula, que foram para o segundo turno.

No post, Trump também utilizou a rapidez da apuração brasileira para criticar as eleições internas nos EUA, ao citar uma demora na contagem de votos em cidades democratas.

"125 milhões de pessoas votaram hoje no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial do Brasil. Os resultados saíram pouco depois do encerramento da votação, NO MESMO DIA! Em Detroit, Filadélfia, Califórnia e várias outras cidades e estados dos EUA, os resultados, com números muito menores, muitas vezes levam semanas para serem fraudados — quer dizer, calculados. A votação nos Estados Unidos é CORRUPTA!!!", afirmou Trump em sua rede social Truth Social.

A fala de Trump sobre o cenário interno dos EUA, em que as cidades que ele citou são estritamente governadas pelos democratas, pode ser interpretada como parte de sua campanha de pressão rumo aos midterms. Nas eleições de meio de mandato no país norte-americano, seu partido, o republicano, busca manter o controle do Congresso.

Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Evaristo Sá/AFP e Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Em uma eleição presidencial marcada pela consolidação da polarização entre bolsonarismo e petismo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no próximo dia 25 de outubro.

Flávio obteve 47,03% dos votos válidos, ou 56.104.503 em números absolutos. Já Lula teve 45,16% dos votos, ou 53.879.538, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE)

Daqui a três semanas, os eleitores voltam às urnas para definir se Flávio Bolsonaro governará o país pelos próximos quatro anos ou se Lula terá um quarto mandato presidencial .

Se Flávio for eleito, tomará posse, aos 45 anos, no dia 5 de janeiro de 2027, na cadeira ocupada por seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, entre 2019 e 2022. Se vencer, Lula assumirá o quarto mandato aos 81 anos e será o primeiro brasileiro a presidir o país quatro vezes.

"Bom, é uma grande vitória. Muito apertada, mas impressionante, na verdade", afirmou.

"Estamos de olho em tudo e vamos observar esta eleição de muito perto", afirmou, na última sexta (2).

articles.title: Ao lado de Nikolas Ferreira, Tarcísio diz que vai 'mergulhar de cabeça' na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: No Palácio dos Bandeirantes, em São Paulo, governador afirmou que pretende ajudar a definir estratégia para ampliar votação do candidato do PL no estado e organizar eventos durante o segundo turno.
articles.summary: No Palácio dos Bandeirantes, em São Paulo, governador afirmou que pretende ajudar a definir estratégia para ampliar votação do candidato do PL no estado e organizar eventos durante o segundo turno.
articles.body:
Tarcísio de Freitas e o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), afirmou nesta segunda-feira (5) que vai se dedicar à campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial. Ao lado do deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), no Palácio dos Bandeirantes, Tarcísio disse que vai “mergulhar de cabeça” na campanha e ajudar a definir estratégias para ampliar a votação do candidato no estado.

“Nós vamos mergulhar de cabeça. Vamos construir juntos essa estratégia, verificar quais são os locais, os territórios onde a gente pode melhorar”, afirmou Tarcísio, após receber o parlamentar que, pela segunda vez, se tornou o deputado federal mais votado do Brasil.

Flávio terminou o primeiro turno à frente de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. No estado de São Paulo, a vantagem foi um pouco maior. Segundo dados do TSE, o candidato do PL teve 51,93% dos votos válidos no estado, contra 38,20% de Lula.

Tarcísio afirmou que a campanha vai analisar os resultados por regiões para identificar onde é possível ampliar a vantagem de Flávio.

“A gente vai pegar onde tem oportunidade de melhoria, vamos organizar os eventos, vamos organizar aí as nossas manifestações, mostrar qual é a agenda pro Brasil”, disse.

“Sem dúvida, tem margem para [Flávio] crescer aqui [em São Paulo], como tem margem pra crescer em outros estados. Nós vamos fazer esse grande trabalho."

Ao lado de Tarcísio, Nikolas Ferreira afirmou que pretende participar da organização da campanha nacional de Flávio. Segundo ele, o planejamento deverá definir regiões prioritárias e buscar votos tanto em estados onde o candidato do PL teve bom desempenho quanto em locais onde Lula ficou à frente.

O deputado disse ainda que vai se reunir com integrantes do PL em Brasília nesta quarta-feira (7) para discutir a estratégia.

“Agora eu acho que a estratégia é ver como, por exemplo, Minas Gerais, Juiz de Fora, que foi a cidade macro que o Bolsonaro perdeu. Então a gente vai ser bastante estratégico”, afirmou.

Nikolas também afirmou que a campanha deverá buscar os votos de eleitores indecisos e ampliar a votação de Flávio no Norte e no Nordeste.

Durante a conversa no Palácio dos Bandeirantes, o deputado ainda criticou institutos de pesquisa e afirmou que pretende propor uma CPI para investigar levantamentos eleitorais.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsorano (PL) — Foto: Reprodução/Ricardo Stuckert/Vittor Sales

Em uma eleição presidencial marcada pela consolidação da polarização entre bolsonarismo e petismo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no próximo dia 25 de outubro.

A confirmação de que haverá segundo turno foi anunciada pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) neste domingo (4), às 20h56, quando 96,78% das urnas já tinham sido apuradas. Àquela altura, Flávio Bolsonaro tinha 47,39% dos votos, e Lula, tinha 44,74%.

Daqui a três semanas, os eleitores voltam às urnas para definir se Flávio Bolsonaro governará o país pelos próximos quatro anos ou se Lula terá um quarto mandato presidencial .

Se Flávio for eleito, tomará posse, aos 45 anos, no dia 5 de janeiro de 2027, na cadeira ocupada por seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, entre 2019 e 2022.

Se vencer, Lula assumirá o quarto mandato aos 81 anos e será o primeiro brasileiro a presidir o país quatro vezes.

articles.title: Anthony Garotinho: TSE aguarda PGE sobre desistência de recurso | G1
articles.standfirst: Prazo para manifestação é de até dois dias. Em decisão, ministro Floriano Marques ainda julgou prejudicado o pedido de tutela de urgência de Anthony Garotinho. Candidato teve 3,17% dos votos válidos para governador. Retotalização de votos pode definir eleição a favor de Douglas Ruas (PL).
articles.summary: O ministro Floriano Marques solicitou parecer da PGE sobre a desistência de Anthony Garotinho, movimento que pode garantir a vitória de Douglas Ruas no primeiro turno.
articles.body:
O ministro Floriano Marques, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) determinou que a Procuradoria-Geral Eleitoral se manifeste em até dois dias sobre o pedido de desistência apresentado pelo ex-governador Anthony Garotinho ( Republicanos ) no recurso contra o indeferimento de sua candidatura ao governo do Rio de Janeiro .

Garotinho desistiu do recurso nesta segunda-feira , depois do primeiro turno das eleições. O ministro, porém, não homologou a desistência de imediato. Ele determinou o envio do processo à PGE, que terá dois dias para se manifestar tanto sobre o recurso quanto sobre o pedido de desistência.

Na decisão, Floriano Marques também considerou prejudicado o pedido de tutela de urgência apresentado por Garotinho.

O candidato havia pedido, entre outras medidas, a manutenção dos direitos de sua candidatura enquanto o recurso estivesse em análise, incluindo acesso ao Fundo Partidário e ao Fundo Eleitoral , propaganda eleitoral gratuita e manutenção do nome na urna.

Segundo o ministro, esse pedido perdeu o objeto após a realização do primeiro turno.

O ministro registrou ainda que o TRE-RJ havia indeferido, por unanimidade, o registro da candidatura de Garotinho por falta de condições de elegibilidade relacionadas ao pleno exercício dos direitos políticos e à filiação partidária, além da incidência de uma causa de inelegibilidade prevista na Lei da Ficha Limpa.

Garotinho teve 274.411 votos, o equivalente a 3,17% dos votos , segundo o sistema de divulgação de resultados da Justiça Eleitoral.

A decisão pode mudar o resultado da eleição no estado e dar a vitória a Douglas Ruas ( PL ) ainda no primeiro turno ( entenda ).

Em entrevista coletiva, Garotinho leu uma carta escrita no domingo (4) na qual disse se sentir "perseguido" e que há anos vem "denunciando o apodrecimento das instituições do Estado, que foram capturadas pelo crime e a corrupção".

"A votação de hoje [domingo] representou a consagração dos corruptos, grande parte reeleita para Alerj [Assembleia Legislativa] e a Câmara Federal.

Após acusações contra Ruas e o seu concorrente, Eduardo Paes (PSD), que disse terem "cúmplices no alto escalão", Garotinho negou apoio em um eventual segundo turno, criticou o voto dos eleitores fluminense e afirmou:

"Em função do resultado manifestado pela população nas urnas, não me resta outra opção jurídica a não ser desistir, de forma livre, expressa, consciente e irretratável. Que agora o povo arque com as consequências do que eles fizeram", disse.

O ex-governador disse também que faria a desistência do recurso mesmo se Paes estivesse na frente e fosse o beneficiado pela vitória no primeiro turno. "Teria até mais prazer se fosse com ele."

Garotinho afirmou ainda que "milicianos, corruptos e políticos aliados ao tráfico tiveram votação expressiva "e disse que Ministério Público, Justiça Eleitoral e polícias Civil e Federal teriam conhecimento de irregularidades.

A defesa de Garotinho protocolou no TSE um termo de desistência do recurso ordinário eleitoral que discutia o registro da candidatura. O processo está sob relatoria do ministro Floriano de Azevedo Marques.

No documento, protocolado às 14h09, os advogados afirmam que a decisão de Garotinho é “livre, expressa, consciente e irretratável” . Os advogados citam o artigo 998 do Código de Processo Civil e sustentam que Garotinho pode desistir do recurso a qualquer momento, sem necessidade de concordância das demais partes.

O resultado, no entanto, ainda depende da formalização da desistência e de uma eventual retotalização pela Justiça Eleitoral . O tribunal ainda não se posicionou .

"Eu fiz a minha parte. Se vai dar, se não vai dar, é um julgamento marcado lá. Eu fiz questão de fazer [protocolar] hoje cedo", disse Garotinho.

Com 100% das urnas apuradas, Ruas teve 4.271.199 votos e apareceu com 49,27% dos votos válidos . Eduardo Paes (PSD), segundo colocado, recebeu 3.706.984 votos, ou 42,76%. Garotinho teve 274.411 votos, equivalentes a 3,17%.

Sem os votos de Garotinho na base de cálculo, o percentual dos candidatos subiria, e Ruas ultrapassaria os 50% necessários para vencer a eleição no primeiro turno. Se os votos forem considerados nulos, porém, nada muda.

O TSE não se posicionou sobre o que será feito caso o pedido de Garotinho seja aceito.

Garotinho votou em colégio na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Guilherme Vizane/ TV Globo

Com os votos de Garotinho, a totalização reúne 8.669.038 votos distribuídos entre os nove candidatos. O resultado com 100% das urnas apuradas, ficou assim (só os três primeiros colocados):

Douglas Ruas (PL): 49,27% — 4.271.199 votos

Eduardo Paes (PSD): 42,76% — 3.706.984 votos

Garotinho (Republicanos): 3,17% — 274.411 votos, anulados sub judice

Nesse cenário, Ruas fica abaixo dos 50%, e os dois candidatos mais votados são convocados para o 2º turno. Sem os 274.411 votos de Garotinho, a base da totalização cairia de 8.669.038 para 8.394.627 votos .

Com os mesmos votos recebidos pelos outros candidatos, mas uma base menor para o cálculo dos percentuais, os números sobem, e o cenário ficaria assim:

Douglas Ruas (PL): 50,88% — 4.271.199 votos

Eduardo Paes (PSD): 44,16% — 3.706.984 votos

Nesse segundo cenário, Ruas ultrapassa os 50% e teria votos suficientes para vencer a eleição no primeiro turno.

O processo de registro de candidatura de Garotinho foi indeferido pelo TRE-RJ por conta de uma condenação por improbidade administrativa. A defesa do ex-governador argumenta que o período de inelegibilidade teria se encerrado em julho — e recorreu.

O recurso foi apresentado ao próprio TRE-RJ, que colhe parecer do Ministério Público Eleitoral e de outros interessados na ação — entre elas a coligação de Eduardo Paes — e remete à corte superior.

Este é o processo que define a validade ou não dos votos dados a Garotinho.

Em outra frente, o ex-governador entrou no TSE para garantir sua campanha mesmo com o indeferimento da candidatura. Foi nesse processo que o ministro Floriano Marques decidiu, na última sexta-feira (2), que os votos dados a Garotinho não deveriam ser considerados.

No domingo, no entanto, o presidente do TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, determinou que os votos dados a Garotinho fossem “considerados no cálculo dos percentuais obtidos por cada concorrente ao pleito majoritário, até que seja proferida decisão colegiada pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral”.

articles.title: Trump culpa ataques da Ucrânia à Rússia por preços altos da gasolina | G1
articles.standfirst: Faltando menos de um mês para as eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA, o presidente dos EUA tentou negar que a guerra do país com o Irã ainda seja a razão para que o combustível siga pesando no bolso dos consumidores.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA tentou negar que a guerra do país com o Irã ainda seja a razão para que o combustível siga pesando no bolso dos consumidores.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , culpou os ataques ucranianos a refinarias de petróleo russas pelos altos preços da gasolina, nesta segunda-feira (5).

Em um post na rede Truth Social, Trump, que vive um momento tenso faltando menos de um mês para as eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA - quando os americanos irão escolher seus representantes do Congresso -, tentou negar que a guerra do país com o Irã ainda seja a razão para que o combustível siga pesando no bolso dos consumidores.

Trump também acusou governadores democratas de influenciarem no valor fechando refinarias em seus estados.

"O que está impulsionando o preço da gasolina não é mais o Estreito de Ormuz, porque números recordes de barris estão sendo exportados quase diariamente, mas sim a palavra 'refinarias'. As refinarias russas estão sendo destruídas pela Ucrânia e as nossas estão sendo fechadas em estados democratas, como a Califórnia, pelos democratas", afirmou.

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, durante lançamento do America.gov — Foto: Mark Schiefelbein/AP

Por que a exportações de petróleo subiram, mas o preço não diminui?

Desde o início da guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irã, o mercado acompanha de perto os efeitos do conflito sobre o preço do petróleo.

As interrupções na produção e no transporte aumentaram o temor de falta de oferta, principalmente por causa do Estreito de Ormuz, uma das principais rotas para o petróleo produzido no Oriente Médio.

Oito meses depois, após tentativas frustradas de acordo de paz, o petróleo voltou a subir mesmo com a reabertura da rota. Na quinta-feira (1º), o Brent, referência internacional, superou novamente US$ 100 por barril.

Em meio ao conflito, as exportações do Golfo Pérsico , área marítima do Oriente Médio que concentra grandes produtores de petróleo, começaram a se recuperar e chegaram a 23,3 milhões de barris por dia na última semana de setembro, segundo estimativa do Goldman Sachs. O volume está próximo da média de 2025.

O que aconteceu com o petróleo durante a guerra?

O conflito entre EUA e Irã aumentou a preocupação com o fornecimento da commodity , uma vez que o Oriente Médio concentra alguns dos maiores produtores de petróleo do mundo.

O principal ponto de atenção foi o Estreito de Ormuz, passagem que liga o Golfo Pérsico ao Golfo de Omã e é usada para transportar petróleo produzido por países como Arábia Saudita, Irã, Iraque, Kuwait e Emirados Árabes Unidos.

Quando o transporte pela região foi afetado, surgiu o temor de que menos petróleo chegasse ao mercado internacional . Isso fez os preços subirem mesmo antes de uma falta efetiva do produto, já que compradores e investidores passaram a considerar o risco de uma interrupção prolongada.

🔎 A alta do petróleo afeta a economia porque encarece combustíveis como gasolina e diesel e também aumenta o custo do transporte de pessoas e mercadorias. Esse repasse pode pressionar os preços de outros produtos e contribuir para uma inflação maior.

Com a recuperação do transporte pelo estreito, parte dessa preocupação diminuiu, mas não desapareceu completamente.

Por que o petróleo não caiu junto com a retomada das exportações?

Um dos motivos para a alta persistente é que a recuperação do mercado de petróleo não aconteceu de forma igual em toda a cadeia.

O petróleo bruto voltou a circular em volumes próximos dos níveis anteriores, mas os combustíveis já refinados, como diesel, gasolina e querosene de aviação , continuam com exportações abaixo do normal.

🔎 Isso acontece porque o conflito também afetou refinarias e aumentou os riscos para o transporte desses produtos. Assim, pode haver petróleo bruto disponível, mas ainda existir dificuldade para transformá-lo em combustíveis e levá-los até os consumidores.

Para Felipe Sant'Anna, analista da Axia Investing, é importante separar essas diferentes etapas. “Uma coisa é a produção, outra coisa é o refino, outra coisa é a mobilidade, a exportação, seja por oleodutos ou seja mesmo por navios petroleiros”, afirma.

Estoques baixos mantêm pressão sobre o petróleo

Segundo a Agência Internacional de Energia (IEA), os estoques globais de petróleo caíram 507 milhões de barris desde fevereiro.

No mesmo período, países-membros liberaram mais de 300 milhões de barris de suas reservas de emergência . Com os estoques baixos, empresas e governos podem aumentar as compras para formar reservas de segurança, mantendo os preços pressionados.

Mesmo com a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz, o mercado ainda considera o risco de novos problemas no abastecimento.

Uma nova escalada da guerra ou ataques a instalações de produção, refinarias e navios poderiam reduzir a oferta e elevar novamente os preços.

“Essas tensões que nós temos e essa incerteza fizeram com que muitos países guardassem petróleo para si e não quisessem mais ‘abrir essa torneira’ para o mundo, o que faz com que os investidores precifiquem os contratos futuros de petróleo para cima”, diz Sant'Anna.

A chegada do inverno no Hemisfério Norte também pode pressionar os preços da matéria-prima, já que aumenta o consumo de energia nos EUA e na Europa.

“Quando o inverno chegar no hemisfério norte, o consumo de energia e principalmente energia de petróleo, né, gás natural, petróleo e derivados, vai aumentar muito”, afirma o analista.

O governo alemão anunciou cortes nos impostos sobre gasolina e diesel para aliviar o impacto da alta dos combustíveis sobre consumidores e empresas. — Foto: Reuters

O que precisa acontecer para o petróleo voltar a cair?

articles.title: Court of Appeal reserves judgement over Drumcree dispute
articles.summary: The deadlock over the Orange Order march in Portadown - opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - has lasted since last Sunday morning.
articles.body:
The Court of Appeal has reserved judgement in a bid by Garvaghy Road residents to challenge a decision to allow a controversial Orange Order parade to go down the predominantly nationalist road.

The deadlock over the proposed march in Portadown, County Armagh - opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - has lasted since Sunday 27 September.

The stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland, with stand-offs in the mid-to-late 1990s accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

Three judges listened to almost four hours of legal arguments inside a packed courtroom in Belfast on Monday.

Residents are appealing a High Court judge's decision, made on 27 September , to refuse them leave to apply for a judicial review.

At the end of Monday's hearing, Lady Chief Justice Dame Siobhan Keegan said the judges would work to a "swift timeframe" but could not give a date for their decision.

Earlier, a lawyer representing Breandán Mac Cionnaith of the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition argued that the Parades Commission decision was flawed.

She said the commission "misdirected itself" when it came to assessing the potential for disorder as a result of the parade.

The lawyer added the approval of the parade has now expired - but said that the case was about whether or not the original decision was lawful.

On 25 September, the Parades Commission decided that the march could go ahead two days later with restrictions in place.

But the parade, from Drumcree Church into Portadown, did not happen due to a large protest on the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road .

First minister rejects call to resign over Drumcree row

During the first hour of the court proceedings on Monday, lawyers focused on the 12-page document published by the Parades Commission on 25 September announcing its approval of the parade and its reasons behind the decision.

At the centre of the case is how the commission dealt with the information it received from the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) ahead of the planned parade.

The residents' lawyer argued that the police's assessment of the potential for disorder was "much more nuanced" than outlined in the document, and the commission should have come to a different decision on the parade.

A lawyer for the Parades Commission told the court that the commission had not made a legal error in reaching its decision.

Speaking after the hearing on Monday, Mac Cionnaith said the residents' lawyers "were very clear on what the situation was in relation to the parade" and he did not think they had "anything to regret so far".

Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) MP Carla Lockhart reiterated that the 35 Orangemen from the Portadown District were "no threat to anyone".

"We will continue to abide by the law," she said outside the court.

"It is a difficult day in Northern Ireland whenever we see law-breakers trying to flout and use the courts again... [it] really is quite staggering."

Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) leader Jim Allister told reporters: "This week we have seen the rule of law on trial and it has been the rule of law against mob rule."

Earlier, a large crowd gathered outside the court that, at its peak, included about 250 people.

At various points, members of the Orange Order delegation were the subject of heckles and abuse.

Comments were directed towards Lockhart and Allister as they arrived and left court.

As the Orange Order's legal adviser Jamie Bryson began speaking at a press conference after proceedings, a member of the crowd shouted over him.

The abuse directed at Lockhart over the past week was addressed by Bryson as he spoke to media.

He said: "The abuse this woman has taken is absolutely vile. This woman now requires protection."

Lockhart said she would not be deterred by the abuse, adding that she would continue "standing up for Portadown Orange District LOL Number One who deserve the right to fulfil their determination to walk the Garvaghy Road".

What was the reaction on the Garvaghy Road?

Protesters have maintained a presence along the road for eight days, with those gathered there on Monday saying they were prepared to stay.

"I knew in my heart there would be no decision today," said Aileen Murray Marshall.

"I'm here for my grandchildren. Parents, fathers and grannies don't want this. It's like point scoring."

Marie-Therese Murray, who was outside the Court of Appeal earlier, said she just wanted everything to go back to normal.

Her 12-year-old son died after being struck by a car on the Garvaghy Road at the height of the dispute in the 1990s.

"It's my son's anniversary next Saturday, 30 years," she said.

"I just want it all to stop, for both Catholic and Protestant children. I don't want to see 1996 back all over again. Please stop".

Singer-songwriter Damien Dempsey became the latest musician to visit the protest site, after Beoga, the Mary Wallopers and Kneecap, when he performed a set on Monday afternoon.

He told BBC News NI that he was visiting to "support the great community here", and introduced himself to the crowd by saying it was "an honour and a privilege" to be there.

articles.title: Israeli medical workers who treated Oct 7 wounded relive day terror hit home
articles.summary: Nil Kirsht-Levi's sister was taken hostage on Oct. 7 as Soroka Medical Center received 674 wounded in 24 hours with just 40 seconds between.
articles.body: As Israel marks three years since the Oct. 7, 2023 terrorist attacks, stories of bravery and self-sacrifice continue to emerge from within a nation grappling with recovery and rehabilitation. For Nil Kirsht-Levi, the three years since the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, massacre have been defined by devastating personal loss, an agonizing wait for her sister who was taken hostage and brought to Gaza and an unwavering commitment to caring for fellow survivors of the cross-border terror attack. Kirsht-Levi, a nurse with Israel's largest healthcare provider, Clalit Southern District, who lives in Kibbutz Magen, spent the morning of Oct. 7 treating patients remotely from her safe room while trying to protect her three children as terrorists invaded the community and went from house to house. At the same time, she desperately texted her sister, Rimon Buchshtab-Kirsht, who lived with her husband in nearby Kibbutz Nirim. FREED HOSTAGE ROM BRASLAVSKI DETAILS ABUSE, STARVATION DURING 738 DAYS IN GAZA CAPTIVITY "I lost more than 30 patients that day, more than 200 people I knew, and around 100 people I knew were kidnapped," Kirsht-Levi told Fox News Digital. "I’m lucky to have a job that saves me, healthy children, a healthy husband. We work every day to recover and rehabilitate ourselves. Every day, we fall and get back up, but we are here — for ourselves, for others and we have won," she continued. "We should never forget, but we must move forward, live every moment and keep going. It’s a privilege to be alive," she added. On Oct. 7, Kirsht-Levi’s sister sent a message saying she could hear Arabic and that terrorists had entered her home. Weeks of agonizing uncertainty followed before Kirsht-Levi saw her sister alive in a Hamas video. She had campaigned for her release and ultimately welcomed her home 53 days later, emaciated and covered in scars, as part of a ceasefire deal in November 2023. Her sister's husband, her brother-in-law, Yagev Buchshtab however, had been murdered by the terrorists. During the 2023 Palestinian terror assault, launched on the Jewish holiday of Simchat Torah, Michaela Koretsky, a midwife with Clalit’s Southern District, improvised lifesaving treatments for wounded members of Kibbutz Alumim. Like so many others, Koretsky was jolted awake by air raid sirens at 6:29 a.m. that fateful day, as Hamas launched thousands of rockets at Israel, providing cover for terrorists as they crossed the border in the ensuing invasion. She rushed with her husband and children to the shelter, where she received a message from Eran, a member of the kibbutz’s civil defense squad, asking if she was home. Eran then began bringing wounded kibbutz members to her for first aid. ISRAELI OCTOBER 7 SURVIVORS CONQUER TRAUMA ALONGSIDE LEGENDARY ROCK ICONS IN POWERFUL NEW DOCUMENTARY "When they entered the house carrying Amichai, he was covered in blood… I switched into nurse mode," she said. Koretsky had Amichai placed on the floor as they continued to hear gunfire outside the kitchen window. She improvised bandages and prepared an IV while staying in contact with an emergency room doctor from Soroka Medical Center who was also in the kibbutz. He confirmed that Amichai was stable. Then Eyal was brought in. He had been shot, with one of the bullets lodged in his lung. After Koretsky placed him on an IV and administered additional oxygen, it became clear that he needed to be evacuated. "We needed to save lives, so I switched my brain into action mode and did what needed to be done. The whole time I did not think that the terrorists would enter my house. I knew one of my children was afraid they would figure out where the wounded were being taken and come after us, but I told myself, ‘I am protected. It will not happen,’" she told Fox News Digital. Her husband, Tzviki, accompanied by members of the kibbutz’s civil defense squad, reached his car and alone he evacuated the wounded under fire to Netivot, where they were transferred to waiting ambulances. From there, both Amichai and Eyal were taken to Soroka Medical Center for further treatment. Prof. Shlomi Codish, director of the hospital in Beersheba, said he made three lifesaving decisions early on Oct. 7 that shaped the response throughout the day. HAMAS USED SEXUAL VIOLENCE 'DELIBERATELY AND SYSTEMATICALLY' ON OCT 7, COMMISSION REPORT FINDS First, he and his team decided not to send the night shift home, allowing the hospital to begin the day with twice its normal staffing level. At 7:45 a.m., they declared a mass-casualty incident, despite not yet knowing how many wounded would arrive and alerted all available staff to report to the hospital. Finally, they ordered additional blood supplies in anticipation of the surge of casualties. "We usually start the shift with 50 units of blood in our blood bank. By the end of the day, we had given 250 units. If we hadn’t ordered additional blood early that morning, we might have run out and people may have died," Codish told Fox News Digital. Codish said the hospital faced several overwhelming challenges throughout the day, beginning with the sheer number of wounded being brought to the hospital. "In the first 24 hours, we received 674 wounded people. At the peak, we received more than 80 in a single hour, with an average of just 40 seconds between wounded people arriving," he said. "This was one of the largest mass-casualty events resulting from terror in human history. The hospital itself was also under fire, with dozens of incoming missile warnings from the Gaza Strip, while attacks were taking place simultaneously at a very large number of sites," he added. SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER The second challenge was the immediate impact of the invasion on hospital staff themselves. "Everyone who came in left a family at home that was potentially under attack. They got into their cars and drove through air-raid sirens in areas that weren’t protected, at significant personal risk, to come in and save lives," he said. Another major challenge was maintaining care inside the hospital as the number of casualties surged. The hospital began the day at full capacity, forcing staff to quickly free up intensive care beds and operating rooms for incoming patients. With roads around the hospital unsafe, transferring patients to other facilities was not an option in the first hours of the attack, while sending ambulances into the field risked exposing them to Hamas ambushes. "When you see babies or children with direct injuries, that is not something you typically see on a battlefield. We saw elderly people with severe wounds inflicted directly, with no protection," Codish said, reflecting on the brutality he witnessed that day. Two babies suffering from dehydration after their parents were killed, simply waiting to be rescued — I defy anyone to find a word other than ‘evil’ to describe it," he added.

articles.title: Ho Chi Minh city: Twelve arrested for allegedly running cat trafficking ring in Vietnam
articles.summary: The men are accused of stealing around 2,700 cats in Ho Chi Minh City, allegedly to be slaughtered for food.
articles.body:
Twelve men have been arrested in Vietnam after allegedly confessing to stealing and selling around 2,700 cats, Ho Chi Minh City police have said.

Cat traps, fur removal machines and measuring scales were among the items seized during the investigation. The men are suspected of taking the pets to be slaughtered for food.

Police allege the suspects roamed through residential areas in small groups on motorbikes at night to steal the cats.

The men reportedly used pieces of fish as bait, placing traps outside houses where they knew cats were kept, state media reported. Thirteen of the rescued felines have since been returned to their owners.

According to the animal protection organisation Humane World for Animals, an estimated five million dogs and one million cats are captured, stolen, trafficked and slaughtered for meat in Vietnam every year.

The consumption of dog and cat meat is legal in the country, where many restaurants openly advertise it on their menu. But vendors require permits that show the origin of the animals.

Each group allegedly stole an average of four to 10 cats per night, according to a police statement in Ho Chi Minh City police department's official newspaper.

On 8 July, police said they seized 50 cats, two weighing scales, 55 cat traps, 14 bags, 13 mobile phones, seven motorbikes, two fur-removing machines and 6.7 million Vietnamese dong ($257; £195).

The 12 suspects were then brought in for questioning, and police say they confessed to stealing around 2,700 cats.

Of the 50 cats that were seized, 13 have been returned to their owners, while the remaining are being kept at the animal welfare centre HavePaws.

While the consumption of dog and cat meat remains more common in Vietnam than other Asian countries, campaigners say attitudes are changing.

A 2023 survey commissioned by Humane World for Animals found growing public opposition, particularly among younger people and pet owners, with 71% backing a ban on the consumption and trade of cat meat.

In June, more than 400 cats destined for slaughter were rescued after authorities dismantled another alleged feline theft ring, the animal welfare group said.

articles.title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
articles.summary: The vessel's captain was killed and 11 crew members were rescued after the attack on the Turkish-owned ship, Ukraine's leader says.
articles.body:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea.

The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.

Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died.

Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea.

Monday's attack by Russia targeted "a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkey", Volodymyr Zelensky said.

He did not give the location of the ship, but Romania's interior ministry said it had sunk about 30 nautical miles south of its port of Sfantu Gheorghe.

"At around 11:00 (09:00 GMT), Coast Guard border police officers were informed that a fire had broken out on board a commercial vessel located within Romania's exclusive economic zone," the ministry said in a statement.

"Eleven crew members have been rescued. Two deceased persons have also been identified," it added.

Ukraine's president said he had "repeatedly proposed concrete steps to de-escalate the situation and ensure security in the Black Sea" - and other countries had made "relevant proposals" too.

"But Russia consistently chooses terror and sinking civilian vessels instead of normal maritime navigation," Zelensky said.

"Pressure is needed to restore global food security," he added. "And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help."

On Sunday, Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier last week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war which began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

President Vladimir Putin admitted last week Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP.

The Russian leader has also intensified his rhetoric against Western allies of Ukraine - repeating a threat of even using nuclear weapons .

Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said last Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes.

The head of Germany's foreign intelligence Martin Jaeger said on Monday that "Germany is in danger of becoming embroiled in a violent conflict with Russia", which was "waging a shadow war" with the threat of attacks against targets in Germany remaining "real and imminent".

articles.title: Cornell campus police made drug arrest at Chi Phi fraternity house hours before alleged gang rape
articles.summary: Cornell University campus police made a drug arrest at the Chi Phi fraternity house less than 24 hours before an alleged gang rape at a party there.
articles.body: Campus police at Cornell University in New York made a drug arrest at the embattled Chi Phi fraternity house on campus less than 24 hours before seven former members are accused in a new civil lawsuit of gang raping a female classmate, according to the school's crime blotter. The Cornell Daily Sun, an independent campus newspaper at the Ivy League school, resurfaced the daily crime log entry in a new report over the weekend. Campus police responded to the university-owned frat house around 1 a.m. on Oct. 19, 2024, and arrested a student on drug charges, according to the blotter. It does not include specific charges and indicates that "an individual has been referred to the Office of Student Conduct." CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS The blotter does not include details about what type of drug or drugs were involved or whether the arrested individual was a member of Chi Phi. Nor was it immediately clear how the incident was resolved. Fox News Digital reached out to Cornell for comment and did not immediately receive a response. CONVICTED RAPIST WHO PREYED ON WOMEN AT AMERICA'S TOP PARTY SCHOOL FACES RECKONING AFTER COURTHOUSE DASH The fraternity went on to host a party later that day, which stretched into the following morning. That party is identified in the civil lawsuit filed on behalf of an unidentified Jane Doe, who reported allegations of sexual assault to university police on Nov. 8, telling investigators that she was attacked between 11 p.m. on Oct. 19 and 5:45 a.m. on Oct. 20. PENN STATE FRAT COCAINE BUST BLOWS LID OFF WIDER STIMULANT SCOURGE HITTING COLLEGE CAMPUSES — AND BEYOND In Doe's lawsuit, she also alleges she had been pressured into snorting ketamine. Ketamine is an anesthetic with dissociative and hallucinogenic effects, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, which also warns that the drug "has also been used to facilitate sexual assault." THE FRAT OMERTÀ: WHISTLEBLOWER WARNS OF ‘CODE OF SILENCE’ AFTER OLE MISS DEATHS, ALLEGED PENN STATE COKE RING The fraternity would later be suspended on Nov. 8, 2024, the same day Doe reported sex assault allegations to campus police, according to Doe's civil complaint. Separately, vandals smashed windows and painted slogans in red at Day Hall, an administrative building, early Monday, according to images published by the Daily Sun. STUDENTS AT TOP PARTY COLLEGE ON EDGE AFTER RAPE, STRANGULATION REPORTED IN CAMPUS HOUSING "We understand the frustration and strong emotions being expressed across our community," Kyle Kimball, the school's vice president for university relations, told Fox News in a statement. "Those concerns deserve to be heard, but damaging property is not the answer. We are investigating the vandalism at Day Hall and will address it in accordance with University policy and applicable law." Tompkins County prosecutors declined to file criminal charges after Doe first reported the incident to university police in 2024. FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has said Doe's November 2024 sworn statement did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual." SEND US A TIP However, according to a local CBS New York report, there is a transcript of what she later told investigators in a two-day interview on Nov. 14 and 15, where she distinguished an initial consensual encounter from allegations of assault that took place later at the party, reportedly telling them, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped." LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "Nobody knows this information about the transcript and that gives me something to really dig into because that changes the landscape for me," Van Houten told the outlet. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor last week to examine the allegations raised in Doe's lawsuit. Jeremy Saland, the attorney for one of the former fraternity brothers named in the lawsuit, Scott Kretzschmar, told Fox News Digital that his client welcomes "a full and thorough investigation" into Doe's allegations. "Fairness and justice demand it, and she deserves nothing less," Saland said. "Justice also requires that those entrusted with the investigation reach conclusions from the evidence, not from statements made before the evidence has been reviewed. Though Scott has never been accused of rape, he is confident that an objective and honest process will clear him of any criminal wrongdoing." articles.title: In 2025, a 118-acre Tennessee estate sold for $6.8 million with just 1,000 sq ft of living space; after a build-out to 17,078 sq ft with a music studio, helipad and wedding venue, it is back for $19.9 million
articles.summary: Some country estates are designed for quiet weekends. Others seem built for an entire community.
articles.body: Some country estates are designed for quiet weekends. Others seem built for an entire community. Elham Valley, a sprawling 118-acre property outside Columbia, Tennessee, falls firmly into the second category. Once a largely undeveloped retreat with just 1,000 square feet of living space, the estate has undergone a dramatic transformation and is now back on the market for $19.9 millions, states an online report by Realtors. As per the report, the price is nearly three times the $6.8 million it fetched in spring 2025, reflecting an extensive build-out that has turned the property into a fully equipped multigenerational compound. Scroll down to read the uniqueness of the property.From blank canvas to private compoundAccording to Realtor, when Elham Valley was listed in late 2024 for $8.6 million, its built space consisted of a guest cabin and a converted greenhouse with indoor and outdoor kitchens and a loft bedroom. Much of the appeal lay in the land itself. The grounds already included a swimming pool, three ponds, a helipad, a covered bridge and more than three miles of private trails. Multiple potential homesites also offered buyers the chance to develop the estate according to their own vision. The new owners have taken that possibility considerably further. Today, the property contains 17,078 square feet spread across several buildings, creating a self-contained retreat designed to accommodate family, guests, entertainment and wellness, the report adds.A sophisticated main residenceAt the heart of the estate is a 5,574-square-foot main residence positioned on a wooded hillside overlooking a pond. The four-bedroom home has three full bathrooms and two half bathrooms, along with a primary suite featuring its own office area. The interiors lean towards understated luxury, combining white oak floors, Venetian plaster, stone walls and vaulted ceilings. Custom cabinetry adds a tailored feel, while a striking stove capable of burning both gas and wood serves as a focal point. A bonus room with a full bar and folding glass doors expands the home's entertaining potential, opening the interiors towards the surrounding landscape, the details of the property reads on Realtor website.Built for music, guests and wellnessThe main house is only one part of the estate. The compound also includes a car barn containing a dedicated music studio, a climate-controlled animal barn, a guest house, a guest cottage with its own pool, a casita with an outdoor pavilion and a wellness centre. The arrangement makes the property unusually versatile. It can function as a family retreat, a private gathering place or an expansive hospitality-style destination without compromising the privacy of the main residence, the report explains too.Outside, the landscape is equally elaborate. Gardens, stocked ponds, spring-fed creeks and walking trails connect the various structures, while mature hardwoods and rolling hills give the property the feel of a secluded European countryside, the report adds.A private venue with room to growElham Valley also comes with commercial potential. The property has received a zoning special exception allowing up to 30 events each year. Dedicated bridal and groom suites, together with indoor and outdoor spaces designed for ceremonies and celebrations, make weddings an obvious use. The existing helipad and extensive grounds add another layer of appeal for large gatherings. Security has also been built into the compound, with a guarded entrance, gated access points, video surveillance and outdoor sound systems. Also, an additional water well and a homesite capable of accommodating a four- to five-bedroom residence offer future owners another opportunity to enlarge the compound. articles.title: Nigeria launches rescue after military plane crashes with 32 aboard
articles.summary: Nigeria launches rescue operation after military aircraft carrying 32 people crashes in Ondo state.
articles.body:
Nigeria has launched a search-and-rescue operation after a military aircraft carrying 32 people crashed in Ondo state in the country’s southwest.

The wreckage of the aircraft has been located near the naval base in Igbokoda, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said on Monday. The plane disappeared while flying from Benin to Lagos.

“The wreckage has been located and search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Keyamo said in a statement on social media.

He added that preliminary information indicated that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board.

Air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft at 09:13 local time (0813 GMT). Repeated attempts to reach it by radio were unsuccessful.

The Nigerian air force said the plane was an ATR-42 that had been travelling to Lagos on a routine flight. Rescue teams have been deployed to the crash site.

Keyamo said he had spoken with Nigeria’s Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and offered the Aviation Ministry’s “total cooperation and assistance” in the rescue effort.

Authorities have not yet confirmed any casualties, and it was not immediately clear how badly the aircraft was damaged.

articles.title: Florida school bus crash kills two, including 10th grade student
articles.summary: The crash happened around 6:15 a.m. when the bus was struck by a Chevy Malibu that was heading westbound, the Polk County Sheriff’s Office said.
articles.body: A school bus crash in Central Florida on Monday killed two people, including a 10th grade student, deputies said. According to the Polk County Sheriff’s Office, the crash happened around 6:15 a.m. in Winter Haven when the bus, going eastbound on Old Lucerne Park Road, was struck by a Chevy Malibu that was heading westbound. “Two people have been killed: a 10th Grade girl and an occupant from one of the other vehicles,” the sheriff’s office said on Facebook. Deputies said the crash caused the bus to lose control and tear off its tire, and then it crashed head-on with a Jeep, causing it to overturn. Three other vehicles were involved in the crash. Deputies said that the student who died was on the bus, and the second person was in the Jeep. Their identities were not released. The bus was carrying 39 people, which included 37 high school students, who were on their way to Winter Haven High School. Deputies said the other two people were identified as the bus driver and their 9-year-old daughter. Due to the crash, Lucerne Park Road was closed in both directions. Drivers are urged to take alternate routes.

articles.title: Michelle O'Neill rejects call to resign over Drumcree row
articles.summary: Facing questions in the Stormont assembly, O'Neill said she was "proud" to stand with the residents and "will continue to stand with them".
articles.body:
First Minister Michelle O'Neill has dismissed a call from the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) to resign over her role in protests against the Drumcree parade.

The Sinn Féin vice-president was branded the "first minister of lawlessness" as unionists criticised the demonstrations on Garvaghy Road.

Police are investigating the unlawful protests which blocked an Orange Order march from passing along the mainly nationalist street in Portadown, County Armagh.

Facing questions in the Stormont assembly, O'Neill said she was "proud" to stand with the residents and "will continue to stand with them".

She described the planned Orange march on 27 September as "unwanted, sectarian and triumphalist".

O'Neill was speaking on Monday in response to an urgent question on the Drumcree dispute tabled by DUP assembly member Phillip Brett.

O'Neill returns to Garvaghy Road as police investigate Sunday's 'unlawful protest'

Court of Appeal reserves judgement over Drumcree parade dispute

An uneasy peace – how a week of the Drumcree parade dispute has unfolded

He called on O'Neill to "drop the bravado" and claimed she had shown "utter contempt" for the ministerial pledge of office.

Brett continued: "If you have been found to breach the ministerial code or the law, will you do the decent thing for once and resign as first minister?"

The first minister responded: "Catch yourself on, would be where I would start with that one.

"I'm going to continue to turn up for the people of the Garvaghy Road.

"I'm proud to stand with them and I will continue to stand with them."

Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) assembly member Timothy Gaston accused O'Neill of being the "first minister of lawlessness" over her role in the street protests.

O'Neill replied: "I am the first minister of what is right."

She added that "we won't need to AI it" - a reference to a TUV councillor who posted online an AI image which exaggerated the size of a loyalist rally in Portadown.

DUP assembly member Jonathan Buckley questioned whether O'Neill would "accept and abide by the lawful decision of the courts" when appeal court judges make a ruling on the parade dispute.

The first minister said that "when the law is wrong I will stand firmly against it" and described the planned march as "morally wrong".

O'Neill later said "shame on you" to DUP assembly members over the party's handling of the Drumcree dispute.

"Your party has championed this," she said to DUP members on the opposite benches.

O'Neill flatly rejected a claim from Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) leader Jon Burrows that many people now regarded the first minister as "completely morally bankrupt".

Earlier, Stormont Speaker Edwin Poots raised concerns over the first minister not attending the chamber last week to answer the tabled urgent question.

The DUP assembly member said O'Neill's absence last Monday was "discourteous" to the assembly and the public.

"Members know my views on ministers being accountable to this house on behalf of the people who put us all here," he said.

articles.title: Former Prince Andrew files a legal action to quash warrants that led to searches of his residences
articles.summary: Former Prince Andrew has filed a legal action challenging the warrants that authorized searches at two of his homes earlier this year as British police investigated allegations related to his links to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
articles.body: Former Prince Andrew has filed a legal action challenging the warrants that authorized searches at two of his homes earlier this year as British police investigated allegations related to his links to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. A judicial spokesperson confirmed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had filed a claim with the High Court in London, and a hearing is scheduled for Thursday. Although Andrew receives a private allowance from King Charles III’s, Buckingham Palace source told NBC News that the monarch was not funding his brother’s legal action. “The palace does not have a role in deciding Andrew’s legal strategy or his actions,” the source said, adding that it was “not involved,” in the case. It came after The Daily Telegraph previously reported that Mountbatten-Windsor had asked the court to determine whether Thames Valley Police acted lawfully in searching the former prince’s homes near Windsor Castle and on King Charles III’s Sandringham estate. If the court were to find in Mountbatten-Windsor’s favor, it could prevent authorities from using evidence discovered during the searches in any prosecution of the former prince, attorney Mark Stephens said. Stephens, of the Howard Kennedy firm in London, described the hearing as a preliminary skirmish in the broader legal battle. “I think the most important thing to take away from this is it shows that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and his lawyers are taking this search warrant and the potential for charges extremely seriously,” he told The Associated Press. “And I think that telegraphs that perhaps there’s more of this to come. And perhaps charges will be preferred down the road.” The searches were conducted in February when Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office, after allegations that the former prince shared sensitive information with Epstein during his time as the U.K.’s trade envoy. Police questioned Mountbatten-Windsor for 11 hours before releasing him under investigation, meaning he was neither charged nor exonerated. It was the first time in nearly four centuries that a senior British royal was placed under arrest, underscoring how deference to the monarchy has eroded in recent years. Thames Valley Police said Monday that its investigation was continuing, even as it confirmed that the department was involved in legal proceedings about the search warrants. A department spokesperson declined further comment while those proceedings are underway. The allegations against Mountbatten-Windsor came to light when the U.S. Justice Department released millions of pages of documents from its investigation into sex trafficking by Epstein and his connections to a network of wealthy, powerful men around the world. Mountbatten-Windsor’s relationship with Epstein has been a source of embarrassment to the royal family for more than a decade and forced him to give up royal duties in 2019. But as further revelations began to leak out of the U.S. investigation last year, the king moved to insulate the monarchy from the fallout by stripping his younger brother of his princely title. After Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested, Charles departed from the “never complain, never explain” approach of his late mother, Queen Elizabeth II, and took the unusual step of issuing a statement on the investigation. “Let me state clearly: the law must take its course,” he said at the time. “As this process continues, it would not be right for me to comment further on this matter.”

articles.title: Muslim outreach or message to Akhilesh? How Imran Masood's 'elevation' will test Congress-SP alliance in UP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The new Congress team in Uttar Pradesh has a daunting challenge at hand: to revive the fortunes of the grand-old-party in the 2027 assembly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The new Congress team in Uttar Pradesh has a daunting challenge at hand: to revive the fortunes of the grand-old-party in the 2027 assembly elections. But before the big political test early next year, there is a pressing concern at hand: the alliance dynamics. And to that extent, the Congress appointments send a mixed signal to ally Samajwadi Party.The appointment of MLA Aradhana Misra-Mona, who is perceived close to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, as the new state chief signals the willingness of the Congress for an amicable seat-sharing discussions. More so, as there is already an open war of words between the leaders of the two parties over the seat share. Congress leaders have insisted that division of seats should be based on “respect and equality.” Aradhana Misra-Mona acknowledges that with the 2027 state elections only a few months away, she would have to hit the ground running as her party seeks to regain political space it has steadily lost in the state since 1989.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Masood's strong remarksTo understand why Imran Masood’s high-profile appointment may have caused some unease, here’s a look at some of the statements he has made in the recent past.June In a video on X Imran Masood said that the Congress will no longer accept the formula that SP had applied in 2024 Lok Sabha polls and that the party was preparing to contest 2027 assembly polls on 200 seats in UP.July "Muslims' mosques are being demolished, madrassas are being razed, injustice is being meted out to Muslims, and atrocities are being committed against Dalits. When a wedding procession sets out, there are many drummers, as well as people who dance and sing. Let these people dance and sing. We are focussed on our work.”SP pushbackClearly, very strong statements which have led to equally strong reactions from the Samajwadi Party. Akhilesh has led the pushback for the Samajwadi Party, making it clear that winnability will be the only criteria for division of seats.When asked about Masood’s remarks, Akhilesh once said: “I have nothing to do with the statement given by anyone. If they fight together, they will benefit."Masood and SP leaders have also engaged in open war of words over who, Rahul or Akhilesh, was more capable of leading the fight against the BJP.While a lot of these remarks are posturing for dominance in seat-sharing talks, the fact is that the open fighting between the two allies has the potential to confuse their cadres. He asserts that Masood’s appointment has a much bigger and important messaging for the minorities, something the Congress should have done long ago.“UP has seen a lot of polarisation under the BJP regime. Muslims form 18% of the state’s population. I think Masood’s appointment is a manifestation of Congress actually beginning to do what it should have done a long time ago, to be bold, to embrace the fact that the minorities are vulnerable under the BJP, that the Muslims need representation, and to stand for them by having a representative who is going to be a working president. articles.title: British Museum boss 'sorry' for Bayeux Tapestry visitor issues
articles.summary: Changes to how visitors see the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition were made after concerns over long queues and overcrowding.
articles.body:
The head of the British Museum has apologised for the experience some visitors have had at its blockbuster Bayeux Tapestry exhibition.

The London institution has announced changes to how visitors see the historic work over concerns of overcrowding.

"Anyone that doesn't have a good experience, we're really sorry about that and we want to put it right," Nicholas Cullinan told the BBC's culture and media editor Katie Razzall.

The new plans include longer opening hours, an audio guide, additional seating and clearer signage.

Some people reported waits of up to two hours. Last week, hundreds of ticket holders were reportedly turned away due to backlogs when the museum closed early for a private event.

"You don't want anyone that comes to see it to have a bad experience, so our focus is very much on getting it right and learning lessons," Cullinan said.

"Obviously we want everyone that comes to have a fantastic experience. To put it into context, we're three weeks into the exhibition run. Next week, we'll hit our 100,000th visitor, which is a pretty extraordinary statistic. The vast number of visitors report having a very good experience."

Asked if the museum team had asked the embroidery's home museum in Bayeux for advice on queue management and timings, Cullinan said they had.

He also denied the museum had let too many people book tickets and said that the issues arose because visitors want to spend more time with the work than expected.

The problem "isn't just the interest, it's that people want to spend more time than anticipated. And that's a good thing. We want people to come and enjoy it, but it means we have to adjust accordingly and that's what we're doing," Cullinan said.

Some visitors have been spending longer than their allocated 40-minute slot viewing the tapestry, meaning others have to move through more quickly, he said.

British Museum announces changes to ease Bayeux Tapestry queues

Bayeux Tapestry arrives in UK for first time in 900 years under police guard

Bayeux Tapestry unveiled to UK public for first time at British Museum

While the museum is reimbursing those who have been turned away, when asked if they might also compensate people for travel costs, Cullinan said it was "a possibility", but added that "obviously this is an incredibly expensive exhibition to mount."

The exhibition has also faced some criticism over accessibility, but Cullinan said they had done "everything they could", given the stipulation that the tapestry had to be laid flat, making it more difficult for wheelchair users to see.

Demand for the exhibition has been high since tickets first went on sale in July, with a record 100,000 sold on the first day.

Members of the public who were not successful in the first ticket release will have two further chances to view the masterpiece when additional tickets go on sale in October and January.

Adult tickets cost £33 during peak times and £27 at off-peak hours, compared to the €12 (£10) fee to see the tapestry in its home in Bayeux, Normandy. Children under 16 can visit the London exhibition for free.

The 70m-long Bayeux Tapestry depicts 58 scenes outlining the extraordinary events surrounding the Norman conquest of England, the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and the end of Anglo-Saxon rule in Britain.

Despite its name, the work is an embroidery rather than a tapestry and contains approximately 626 human figures and 200 horses.

The Bayeux Tapestry is on loan from the French government, having been transported from its home in Normandy - where it has been exhibited since 1983. It will be on display until July 2027.

The loan marks the first time the tapestry has returned to the UK since it was created more than 900 years ago.

articles.title: Prisoner took his own life after terror order had 'substantial impact' on mental state, inquest finds
articles.summary: Akhtar Uddin was jailed for breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures in 2020.
articles.body:
A prisoner took his own life after strict terrorism control measures imposed by the government had a "substantial impact" on his mental state, an inquest jury has concluded.

Akhtar Uddin, 35, a builder from east London, died in HMP Wandsworth on Christmas Day 2021 after being jailed the previous year for breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPIM).

The jury at Inner West London Coroner's Court also found the prison service had failed to provide the support that Uddin needed.

Jurors concluded that Uddin died due to an action he took but said that it was "not possible to determine whether he intended the outcome to be his death".

First alleged neo-Nazi under special terror powers

The powers being used to disrupt a terror group

Prior to being jailed in February 2020 for breaching the TPIM order, Uddin had served a sentence for racially or religiously aggravated harassment.

TPIMs allow the authorities to control people whom the government believes are involved in terrorism, but who are not facing criminal charges. The home secretary acts on advice from MI5 when imposing TPIMs.

Subjects of TPIMs face measures such as wearing an electronic tag, curfews, relocation to a different part of the country, bans on internet use, controls on finances, and limits on who they can meet and where they can go.

Breaches can result in a terrorism conviction and prison sentence. TPIMs can currently last up to five years, up from a maximum of two years when Uddin was under one.

Uddin breached the measures 12 times by withdrawing more money than he was permitted. The inquest heard he largely spent it on drugs. He had over 20 previous criminal convictions - none of which were for terrorism offences.

The inquest, which was the first ever to consider the impact of TPIMs, heard that Uddin believed the order was originally imposed because he had made reckless statements while under the influence of drugs, but that he insisted he was not a terrorist.

It is understood he was alleged to have made verbal threats and associated with people regarded by MI5 as being involved in terrorist activity.

Coroner Bernard Richmond KC said Uddin was "loved and loving" but was "not someone without his troubles" and these revolved around his drug use.

The coroner said he will be issuing a report to the government out of concern about a risk to other people under the terrorism control measures.

When the TPIM was first imposed on Uddin in January 2020, he was forcibly relocated to the West Midlands after being arrested at the prison gates in front of his sister who had come to meet him on release.

The full reasons for a person being on a TPIM are typically kept secret, even from the person subject to the TPIM, because they are based on MI5 intelligence.

The inquest heard that Uddin feared the TPIM would be re-imposed when he left prison early in 2022, and that he would again breach it due to drugs.

Today the inquest jury concluded the following:

"We are satisfied that the imposition of the original TPIM and its unusually restrictive nature had a substantial impact on the mental state of Akhtar Uddin."

"We are satisfied that the fear of a likely reimposition of such a restrictive TPIM, and its possibly never-ending nature, had a significant impact on the mental state of Akhtar in prison."

"We are satisfied, as a result of the consistent evidence that prison services were unaware of TPIM restrictions and their likely impact on Akhtar, there was a failure to provide support most suitably targeted to Akhtar's specific needs and situations."

A governor at HMP Wandsworth accepted in evidence that lack of knowledge of TPIMs by prison staff had resulted in "unintentionally cruel" treatment of Uddin.

Giving evidence, Uddin's sister Jasmine said that, in the weeks before his death, he had described "counter terrorism officers" questioning him in prison and saying he would never get off the TPIM.

A statement from Uddin's family, issued by their solicitors Birnberg Peirce, said they welcomed the inquest's findings.

"Although nothing can bring back their loving son, brother and uncle, they hope that this will make a real difference to those who are currently at the mercy of this inhumane regime."

His former solicitor, Amer Ahmad, had told Uddin in autumn 2021 there were "highly limited prospects" that he would succeed in having the TPIM legally overturned, the inquest heard.

Dr Richard Latham, an NHS consultant forensic psychiatrist, appeared as an expert witness for the coroner and concluded that Uddin had an undiagnosed "personality disorder", associated "psychological problems and vulnerabilities", and this resulted in impulsiveness, grievance and paranoia.

He said Uddin probably assumed the worst about the TPIM in future, and that this prospect would have created "distress and a sense of hopelessness".

Dr Latham added TPIMs are intended to create a "degree of isolation," but that plays on psychological vulnerability and can create "emotional isolation".

Questioned by Jesse Nicholls, representing the bereaved family, Dr Latham said Uddin "felt a sense of injustice" about being branded a terrorist.

The inquest heard there was little or no awareness by staff in HMP Wandsworth of TPIMs. The coroner said "very few people, if any" knew about Uddin's TPIM, the revocation, or potential re-imposition.

In the absence of jurors, the coroner said there was much assessment by the state of Uddin's potential risk to others, but he had seen "nothing" showing any assessment of risks to him. He said there is a "paucity of support for people subject to TPIMs" and there is a potential risk to other people subjected to them.

For this reason, he added, he would be writing a preventing future deaths report.

There has been a trend towards TPIM subjects having mental health issues.

The independent reviewer of terrorism legislation, Jonathan Hall KC, has noted in previous reports that the "Home Office recognises poor mental health as a dominant feature amongst recent TPIM subjects" and that "poor mental health and neurodivergence (autism)" as being in evidence amongst them.

A government spokesperson said TPIMs were "a last resort to manage the risk posed by terrorists who cannot be prosecuted or deported" and are "carefully considered and strictly focused" on stopping a person's "involvement in terrorist activity".

The government was dealing with a prison crisis it "inherited", the spokesperson added, and was improving training to help staff "manage risks of self-harm and suicide".
